sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: As of the Nov 20 close, the S&P 500 sits at 6,910, its lowest close in the past month and about 11% below the 7,757 it started the window at. The Nasdaq 100 is in the same spot at 25,029, roughly 16% under its 1-month high of 29,823. The VIX closed at 35.9, the top of its 1-month range (low 16.6). The Euro Stoxx 50 also sits at its 1-month low, 5,942 vs a high of 6,399. The week carries 27 scheduled reports in the S&P 500 / Russell 1000 / core pool, concentrated in technology (10 names), consumer-cyclical (5) and industrials (4); all dates are estimates.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tuesday is the busiest day: Workday and HP Inc. report into technology, where the median 3-day reaction after recent prints is -0.1% across 810 tickers. Best Buy and Dick's Sporting Goods plug into consumer-cyclical (+0.3% median, 681 tickers). Wednesday has Deere in industrials (+0.3% median). Thursday, Nov 26 is a US market holiday, yet 16 reports carry that estimated date, including Kroger (consumer-defensive, -0.5% median) and Electronic Arts (communication-services, -0.3% median), so expect those dates to move.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: The sectors with the largest median 3-day reactions are mining (+4.6% median, 229 tickers, 2,766 news items), copper (-2.5%, 6 tickers, 231 news items) and energy (+2.0%, 328 tickers, 5,160 news items). None of this week's scheduled reports sit in those three sectors. The sectors that do have reports this week show median reactions within about 0.7% of zero, so recent prints give little directional read.
